20280:
Recall first law \Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W with \Delta Q as heat exchanged
For isothermal temperature is constant so heat flows to do work and for isobaric and isochoric heat changes internal energy or work
By definition an adiabatic change is carried out with no thermal contact so \Delta Q = 0
Hence heat is neither absorbed nor released only in the adiabatic process
→ (B)
20281:
Recall kinetic theory result for an ideal gas where mean translational energy per molecule is \bar{E} = \frac{3}{2} k_{B} T
Raising temperature at fixed volume increases molecular speeds while the number of molecules and hence mass stay fixed
Pressure rises because faster molecules strike walls harder and intermolecular spacing is set by container volume
Thus only the average kinetic energy grows with temperature
→ (B)
20283:
Recall truth tables where AND gives high only for A = 1 and B = 1 while OR gives high for either high
Trace the given circuit where the two inputs first combine and then pass through an inverting stage
The output is therefore Y = \overline{A \cdot B} which stays low only when both inputs are high
This high-except-both-high behaviour is the NAND operation
→ (C)
20286:
Recall shortest path means ground velocity must point due north with zero eastward drift
Let the stroke make angle \theta west of north so westward component is v_{s} \sin\theta
Cancel the eastward river drift with v_{s} \sin\theta = v_{r} giving \sin\theta = \frac{10}{20} = \frac{1}{2}
Thus \theta = 30^{\circ} west of north
→ (A)
20287:
Recall tension plus radial component of weight supplies centripetal force m v^{2} divided by length
At the top weight assists the centre pull while at the bottom weight opposes it so tension must be largest there
Explicitly T_{top} = \frac{m v^{2}}{r} - mg and T_{bottom} = \frac{m v^{2}}{r} + mg
Since tension peaks at the bottom the wire is most likely to break there
→ (C)
20288:
Recall constant A_{0} only shifts the mean position and does not affect oscillation size
Combine the harmonic terms as A \sin\omega t + B \cos\omega t = R \sin(\omega t + \phi)
Squaring coefficients gives amplitude R = \sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2}}
Hence the motion oscillates about A_{0} with that amplitude
→ (B)
20290:
Recall average velocity is total displacement divided by total time over the chosen interval
Over one complete vibration the particle returns to its starting position and phase
So net displacement is zero while the time period T is nonzero
Zero divided by T gives zero average velocity
→ (D)
20293:
Recall steady conduction rate \frac{Q}{t} = k A \frac{\Delta T}{L} where k is thermal conductivity
Rearranging gives k = \frac{(Q/t) L}{A \Delta T} with units of power per length per kelvin
Power unit watt over metre kelvin gives \text{W m}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}
This matches the stated dimensional option
→ (D)
20294:
Recall elastic force grows linearly from zero to Mg as the wire extends by l
Work stored equals area under the load extension graph which is a triangle
Hence U = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{force} \times \text{extension}
Substituting force Mg and extension l gives U = \frac{1}{2} Mgl
→ (C)
20296:
For a quantity built from products and quotients of powers, maximum fractional errors add with each exponent as weight
For X = \frac{A^{2}B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3}D^{3}} the rule gives \frac{\Delta X}{X} = 2\frac{\Delta A}{A} + \frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta B}{B} + \frac{1}{3}\frac{\Delta C}{C} + 3\frac{\Delta D}{D}
Substitution of the given errors gives 2 \times 1 + \frac{1}{2} \times 2 + \frac{1}{3} \times 3 + 3 \times 4 = 2 + 1 + 1 + 12
Total maximum percentage error is therefore 16 percent
→ (B)
20298:
In the visible spectrum wavelength increases in the order violet, blue, green, yellow, orange and red
Red light lies near 620 to 750\text{ nm} while violet lies near 380 to 450\text{ nm}
Hence red has the longest wavelength among the given colours
→ (A)
20301:
Charge on a hollow metal sphere resides entirely on its outer surface with none enclosed inside
By Gauss law the field inside is therefore zero for every r < R
Outside, the sphere acts like a point charge so E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}}\frac{Q}{r^{2}}, which decreases as r increases for r > R

20302:
Eddy currents are circulating currents induced in bulk metal by changing flux and are exploited in induction furnaces and magnetic braking
They also appear in electromagnets where laminated cores are used to suppress them
An electric heater works by ordinary Joule heating I^{2}R in a resistive element, not by induced eddy currents

20304:
Angle of dip is positive when the field points downward into the earth, which occurs in the northern magnetic hemisphere
It is negative when the field points upward out of the earth, which occurs in the southern magnetic hemisphere
Since A has \delta = +25^{\circ} and B has \delta = -25^{\circ}, A lies in the north and B in the south
→ (C)
20306:
A rainbow combines refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in water drops, with one reflection for the primary and two for the secondary
Because of the extra reflection the colour order reverses in the secondary bow
An observer sees it looking away from the sun toward falling rain, so facing the sun and still seeing a rainbow is impossible
→ (C)
20307:
By Ampere law the current enclosed grows as d^{2} inside a uniform solid conductor, giving B = \frac{\mu_{0}Id}{2\pi R^{2}}
Thus B rises linearly from zero at the centre to a maximum at the surface d = R
Outside the conductor the full current is enclosed so B = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi d}, falling hyperbolically
Only the curve with a linear rise followed by a 1/d fall matches
→ (C)
20308:
Angular speed and period are linked by \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}
Both particles complete one circle in the same time period T
Hence their angular speeds are identical whatever their radii or linear speeds
Ratio of the two angular speeds is therefore 1 : 1
→ (D)
20310:
At the interface Snell law gives \mu_{1} \sin i = \mu_{2} \sin r for the refracted ray
As incidence i grows the refracted ray bends toward grazing emergence
Critical incidence i_{c} is defined by the refracted ray just skimming the surface
Grazing emergence means refracted angle r = 90^{\circ}
→ (D)
20312:
A p-type crystal is doped with trivalent acceptor atoms such as boron or indium
Each acceptor creates a vacancy that behaves as a mobile positive hole
Holes far outnumber thermally generated electrons in this material
So holes are the majority carriers with trivalent atoms as dopants
→ (B)
20313:
A protection device must break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit
Conductors, inductors and ordinary switches cannot interrupt such fault current by themselves
A fuse carries a thin element that melts and opens the circuit on overload
Hence the fuse acts as the circuit protection device
→ (D)
20315:
Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance and draws no branch current
Ideal ammeter has zero resistance and drops no voltage across itself
Both meter arrangements therefore reduce to the same battery-resistor loop
Current through the ammeter and drop read by the voltmeter stay identical
Hence V_{1} = V_{2} with i_{1} = i_{2}
→ (C)
20316:
An \alpha-particle is the nucleus of a helium-4 atom emitted in decay
Neutral helium carries 2 protons, 2 neutrons and 2 electrons
Ejection strips away the orbital electrons, leaving only the nucleus
The particle is therefore 2 protons and 2 neutrons only

20320:
Initial magnitudes are +Q and -Q at fixed separation with force F
Transferring 25 percent of A to B leaves q_{A} = 0.75Q on A
Charge on B becomes q_{B} = -Q + 0.25Q = -0.75Q
Force scales with product magnitude 0.75 \times 0.75 = 0.5625 = \frac{9}{16}
New force is therefore \frac{9F}{16} at the same separation
→ (B)
20322:
Three force vectors arranged head to tail in triangle PQR close on themselves
A closed vector polygon has zero resultant so net force on the particle is zero
With no net force acceleration is zero by Newton first law
Velocity therefore keeps its magnitude and direction unchanged
→ (C)
20326:
In hcp the anions set the lattice with one octahedral void per anion
Cations fill 75 percent of these voids, so per 100 anions there are 75 cations
Cation to anion ratio is 75:100 = 3:4
Formula is \text{C}_{3}\text{A}_{4}, which is option D

20328:
Haber synthesis follows \text{N}_{2} + 3\text{H}_{2} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_{3}
Two moles of ammonia need three moles of hydrogen
Scaling to the required amount keeps the same 3 to 2 proportion
Twenty moles of ammonia need 20 \times \frac{3}{2} = 30 moles of hydrogen

20331:
Write the molecular orbital occupancy for the second period diatomics
\text{Be}_{2} has no net bond while \text{O}_{2} and \text{N}_{2} keep one \sigma component in their bond order
\text{C}_{2} with twelve valence electrons fills bonding levels as two \pi units with bond order two

20332:
Draw pent-2-en-4-yne as \text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}=\text{CH}\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}
Carbon skeleton gives four carbon to carbon \sigma bonds

One double bond adds one \pi and one triple bond adds two \pi for a total of three \pi bonds
→ (A)
20333:
Rubidium Z = 37 has configuration [\text{Kr}]5s^{1}, so the valence electron is 5s
Hence n = 5 and l = 0, and with l = 0 the only allowed magnetic value is m = 0
Spin +\frac{1}{2} completes the set 5, 0, 0, +\frac{1}{2}
Option C lists m = 1 which is impossible for l = 0, so option B

20334:
State the d count and ligand field for each complex
[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]^{3-} with \text{Fe}^{3+} is low spin \text{d}^{5} with one unpaired electron
[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_{4}] with \text{Ni}^{0} is tetrahedral \text{d}^{10} and [\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_{4}]^{2-} is square planar \text{d}^{8}, both paired
[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+} with \text{Co}^{3+} is low spin \text{d}^{6} fully paired so only the iron complex is paramagnetic

20336:
In water the basicity of amines reflects electron release plus solvation of the conjugate acid
Methyl groups donate electrons but extra methyls hinder hydration and reduce stabilization
Secondary amine balances both effects best while tertiary amine is least stabilized in water
Order is (\text{CH}_{3})_{2}\text{NH} > \text{CH}_{3}\text{NH}_{2} > (\text{CH}_{3})_{3}\text{N}

20337:
Colloidal \text{AgI} adsorbs the ion present in excess on its surface
A negatively charged [\text{AgI}]\text{I}^{-} sol needs excess iodide ions in solution
Both mixtures with more millimoles of \text{KI} than \text{AgNO}_{3} leave free \text{I}^{-} after precipitation
Mixtures with excess silver give a positive sol while the first two mixtures give the negative sol

20338:
A Bronsted acid donates a proton and its conjugate base is the acid minus \text{H}^{+}
Water loses one proton to give hydroxide
Hydrogen fluoride loses one proton to give fluoride
Conjugate bases are \text{OH}^{-} and \text{F}^{-} respectively

20339:
A basic buffer pairs a weak base with its salt from a strong acid
Hydrochloric acid neutralizes part of ammonium hydroxide to ammonium chloride
With 100\text{ mL} of 0.1\text{ M HCl} and 200\text{ mL} of 0.1\text{ M NH}_{4}\text{OH} excess base remains
Remaining \text{NH}_{4}\text{OH} with formed \text{NH}_{4}\text{Cl} acts as a basic buffer
→ (C)
20340:
Protonation places \text{H}^{+} on the most electron-rich lone pair available in the molecule
Strong electron-withdrawing nitro groups drain electron density by combined -\text{I} and -\text{M} effects
The isomer carrying three nitro groups ortho and para to the donor site has the most depleted lone pair
It is therefore the least basic and the most difficult to protonate

20341:
Partial hydrogenation of \text{H}_{3}\text{C}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_{3} must stop at the alkene stage with syn geometry
Poisoned palladium with \text{H}_{2}, \text{Pd} over \text{C} and quinoline adsorbs the alkyne and delivers both hydrogens from the same face
This syn addition furnishes cis-2-butene selectively
Dissolving metal reduction with \text{Na} in liquid \text{NH}_{3} would instead give the trans isomer

20342:
Small \text{Si}^{4+} is comfortably surrounded by six compact fluoride ions to give [\text{SiF}_{6}]^{2-}
Chloride ions are much larger, so six of them cannot pack around the same small silicon centre
Steric crowding makes [\text{SiCl}_{6}]^{2-} unstable and it is not observed
Larger congeners \text{Ge} and \text{Sn} accommodate six chlorides or hydroxides with ease

20343:
Down the group hydroxides become more ionic and more strongly basic from \text{Mg} to \text{Sr}
Beryllium is exceptional because tiny highly polarising \text{Be}^{2+} makes \text{Be}-\text{O} bonding appreciably covalent
Hence \text{Be}(\text{OH})_{2} dissolves in both acids and alkalis, like alumina
It is the only amphoteric hydroxide in the list
→ (D)
20344:
Aqueous \text{NaOH} first neutralises the phenolic proton with \text{p}K_{a} near 10
The resulting intermediate A is the resonance-stabilised sodium phenoxide \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{O}^{-}\text{Na}^{+}
Subsequent carboxylation acts on this activated phenoxide ring
Only the phenoxide structure matches the listed option

20345:
Both manganate and permanganate place \text{Mn} at the centre of four oxide ligands
A pure sigma framework would leave the short strong \text{Mn}-\text{O} bonds unexplained
Overlap of filled oxygen \text{p}-orbitals with vacant manganese \text{d}-orbitals adds \pi character
This \text{p}_{\pi}-\text{d}_{\pi} bonding stabilises the tetrahedral geometry

20346:
Across period two the general trend rises with nuclear charge, but half-filled and full shells intrude
Beryllium holds a full 2\text{s} shell, so it exceeds boron which loses a higher-energy 2\text{p} electron
Nitrogen holds a half-filled 2\text{p} shell, so it exceeds oxygen where pairing repulsion assists removal
Combining both exceptions gives \text{Li} < \text{B} < \text{Be} < \text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N} < \text{F} < \text{Ne}

20348:
Gaseous \text{PCl}_{5} is trigonal bipyramidal with 120 degree equatorial and 180 degree axial angles
Axial bonds suffer greater repulsion and are measurably longer and weaker
Far from inert, \text{PCl}_{5} is a vigorous chlorinating agent that hydrolyses readily
Calling the molecule non-reactive is therefore the incorrect statement
→ (D)
20349:
Orbital energies follow the \text{n} + \text{l} rule, with higher \text{n} breaking ties
Sums give 4\text{d} = 6, 5\text{p} = 6, 6\text{p} = 7 and 5\text{f} = 8
Hence 5\text{f} lies highest and 6\text{p} follows it
For the tied pair, 5\text{p} with larger \text{n} lies above 4\text{d}, giving 5\text{f} > 6\text{p} > 5\text{p} > 4\text{d}

20350:
Biodegradable polyamides contain amino-acid residues that enzymes can hydrolyse
Nylon 2-nylon 6 is the copolymer of glycine and 6-aminohexanoic acid, so microbes cleave it readily
Nylon-6, nylon-6,6 and Buna-S lack such digestible linkages and persist in the environment
Only nylon 2-nylon 6 qualifies as biodegradable
→ (B)
20351:
\text{XeF}_{4} has two lone pairs trans to each other, giving a square planar shape
\text{XeF}_{6} carries one lone pair on a seven-coordinate centre, giving a distorted octahedron
\text{XeOF}_{4} adopts square pyramidal geometry with oxygen at the apex
\text{XeO}_{3} with three bonds and one lone pair is pyramidal, so the code matches the stated option
→ (B)
20352:
Thermal stability tracks the \text{E}-\text{H} bond strength down group sixteen
Atomic size grows from \text{O} to \text{Po}, so overlap weakens and the bond dissociation enthalpy falls
Decomposition therefore becomes easier in the order \text{H}_{2}\text{O} hardest to \text{H}_{2}\text{Po} easiest
The correct sequence is \text{H}_{2}\text{Po} < \text{H}_{2}\text{Te} < \text{H}_{2}\text{Se} < \text{H}_{2}\text{S} < \text{H}_{2}\text{O}

20353:
\text{Br}_{3}\text{O}_{8} can be viewed as linked bromate-type units joined through bridging oxygen atoms
Only one connectivity gives each bromine its correct terminal \text{Br}=\text{O} count and oxidation state
The remaining options misplace a bridge or leave a bromine with an impossible coordination
The correctly bridged drawing is the listed option

20354:
Ozonolysis cleaves each doubly bonded carbon into a carbonyl fragment
Propanone plus ethanal recombine to the alkene (\text{CH}_{3})_{2}\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_{3}, which is 2-methyl-2-butene
Electrophilic addition of \text{HCl} places \text{H}^{+} to form the more stable tertiary carbocation
Capture by \text{Cl}^{-} then gives the Markovnikov chloride product

20355:
Phosphate transfer enzymes such as kinases bind ATP as its magnesium complex rather than free ATP
Here \text{Mg}^{2+} shields the phosphate negative charges and correctly orients ATP in the active site while beryllium, calcium and strontium cannot perform this role
Hence the required alkaline earth cofactor M is magnesium
→ (B)
20356:
Malachite is a basic copper carbonate mineral containing both carbonate and hydroxide groups
Its formula is \text{CuCO}_{3}\cdot\text{Cu}(\text{OH})_{2} while \text{CuFeS}_{2} is chalcopyrite and \text{Fe}_{3}\text{O}_{4} is magnetite
Plain \text{Cu}(\text{OH})_{2} alone is not malachite so only the basic carbonate matches
→ (D)
20357:
Hydrogen lines ending at n = 1 form the Lyman series in the ultraviolet region
Transitions ending at n = 2 form the Balmer series with wavelengths roughly 400 to 700 nm in the visible region
Paschen ending at n = 3 and Brackett ending at n = 4 lie in the infrared region
→ (B)
20358:
Maximum boiling azeotropes arise from large negative deviation with strong attraction between unlike molecules
Water plus nitric acid shows strong hydrogen bonding and boils higher than either pure component
Ethanol plus water and acetone plus carbon disulphide show positive deviation while heptane plus octane is nearly ideal
→ (A)
20359:
For a galvanic change use \Delta_{r}G^{\circ} = -nF E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ} with spontaneous sign negative
Here 2\text{Fe}^{3+} gains two electrons and 2\text{I}^{-} loses two electrons so the electron count is n = 2
Substitution gives \Delta_{r}G^{\circ} = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.24 = -46320 \text{ J mol}^{-1}
This equals -46.32 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} confirming a spontaneous cell reaction

20360:
Entropy increases when disorder or gas moles increase such as evaporation, sublimation and isothermal expansion
In 2\text{H}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{H}_{2}(\text{g}) two moles of atomic gas combine into one mole of molecular gas
Since the particle count and disorder fall, the entropy change is negative only for this combination

20361:
Pure nitrogen comes from thermal decomposition of sodium azide or barium azide, giving the first pairing
Haber process makes ammonia and Contact process makes sulphuric acid, giving the next two pairings
Deacon process oxidizes hydrogen chloride to chlorine, giving the last pairing
The full code matches the stated option
→ (D)
20362:
Silicon tetrachloride hydrolyses readily and tin tetrafluoride is ionic while germanium tetrahalides exceed dihalides in stability
Lead tetrafluoride pairs highly electronegative fluoride with \text{Pb}^{4+} and is ionic rather than covalent
Covalent character grows with large polarizable halides such as chloride, so calling lead tetrafluoride covalent is incorrect

20363:
Essential amino acids cannot be made in the body and must be supplied through diet
Valine, leucine and lysine belong to the essential set required for growth and repair
Alanine is formed from pyruvate by transamination and is therefore non-essential

20365:
Benzene with chlorine in presence of \text{AlCl}_{3} generates the electrophile \text{Cl}^{+} that attacks the aromatic ring
This yields \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{Cl} + \text{HCl} through aromatic electrophilic substitution
Diazonium replacement with \text{Cu}_{2}\text{Cl}_{2} is Sandmeyer type while benzene with chlorine under UV light is radical addition and benzylic alcohol with HCl is nucleophilic substitution

20366:
Phthalic acid with ammonia first gives ammonium phthalate and then the diamide on heating
Strong heating causes intramolecular cyclization with elimination of two molecules of water
The ring-closed cyclic imide product is phthalimide which corresponds to option B

20367:
For \text{N}_{2} + 3\text{H}_{2} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_{3} each rate is divided by its stoichiometric coefficient
Reactant disappearance carries a minus sign while product formation carries a plus sign
Hence -\frac{d[\text{N}_{2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[\text{H}_{2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\text{NH}_{3}]}{dt}
The nitrogen to ammonia part of this equality matches option C

20368:
In \text{K}_{4}[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}] four potassium ions give +4 so iron is present as \text{Fe}^{2+} with d^{6} configuration
Cyanide written as \text{CN}^{-} is a strong field ligand producing a large octahedral splitting
All six electrons pair in the lower set giving t_{2g}^{6} e_{g}^{0} rather than tetrahedral e and t_{2} notation

20369:
Temporary hardness comes from soluble calcium and magnesium bicarbonates in water
Clark method adds calculated lime which converts them into insoluble carbonates that precipitate out
Calgon, ion-exchange and synthetic resin routes are used for permanent hardness rather than this case

20370:
Viroids are infectious naked RNA molecules without any protein coat
Prions are infectious abnormally folded proteins without nucleic acid
Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites whose infectivity resides in the nucleic acid genome, not the protein coat
Hence the statement that the protein coat is the infective constituent is incorrect

20371:
Purine bases carry a double-ring structure and are adenine and guanine
Pyrimidines carry a single ring and are cytosine, thymine and uracil
Thymine occurs only in DNA and uracil only in RNA
So adenine and guanine are the purines shared by both DNA and RNA

20372:
Glucose enters cells through facilitative GLUT transporters with distinct regulation
GLUT I supplies basal uptake in most cells, GLUT II acts in liver and pancreas, and GLUT III in neurons, all insulin-independent
GLUT IV in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue is stored in intracellular vesicles and translocates to the membrane only on insulin signalling
Hence GLUT IV is the insulin-dependent transporter

20373:
Chief cells secrete pepsinogen and oxyntic cells secrete hydrochloric acid, both of which attack the gut wall
Goblet cells secrete mucin that hydrates into a continuous mucus layer over the epithelium
This mucus barrier shields the lining from acid and proteolytic enzymes
So the protective secretion comes from goblet cells

20374:
Industrial enzyme production needs bulk culture of microbes under sterile aerated and agitated conditions
A BOD incubator holds only small culture plates, a sludge digester treats sewage, and an oven sterilises or dries material
A bioreactor provides a large vessel with controls for pH, temperature, oxygen and stirring for mass growth
Hence large-scale microbial culture uses a bioreactor

20375:
Golden rice is a biofortified transgenic rice developed to supply provitamin A
It carries introduced genes including phytoene synthase from daffodil that rebuild the beta-carotene pathway in the endosperm
The grains therefore accumulate yellow beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A

20376:
In situ conservation protects species within their natural habitats
Biosphere reserves, wildlife sanctuaries and sacred groves all preserve organisms where they naturally occur
A botanical garden maintains plants outside their habitat under human care
That makes it an ex situ method, so it is the non-in situ option

20377:
The mRNA is read in consecutive triplets, so adding or removing bases in multiples of three preserves the downstream frame
Insertion or deletion of a single base, or of two bases at positions 4 and 5, shifts every later codon
Deletion of the three-base block GGU from positions 7, 8 and 9 removes exactly one codon

20378:
Nuclear waste stays radioactive for very long periods and must be isolated from living systems
Shooting it into space, burying it under Antarctic ice or dumping it in the deep ocean risk spread and are unsafe or prohibited
The accepted practice places sealed waste in stable rock formations deep below the land surface

20379:
Lactobacillus converts milk sugar to lactic acid and forms curd
Saccharomyces cerevisiae ferments sugars to carbon dioxide that leavens bread
Aspergillus niger produces citric acid by industrial fermentation
Acetobacter aceti oxidises ethanol to acetic acid
This pairing gives the stated option

20380:
Genetic maps measure separation between loci by recombination frequency

20381:
Intra-uterine devices include inert, copper-releasing and hormone-releasing types

Progestasert and LNG-20 release progesterone-like hormones that thicken cervical mucus and suppress endometrial receptivity

20382:
Biocontrol of plant disease uses living antagonists that parasitise or suppress pathogens

So only Trichoderma serves as a biocontrol agent here

20383:
Expressed sequence tags are short cDNA reads obtained from cellular mRNA
They therefore mark only those genes that are transcribed into RNA in the sampled tissue

20384:
Colostrum is the yellowish secretion released in the first days after delivery

This antibody coats the newborn gut and gives passive mucosal protection before its own immunity matures
Natural killer cells, monocytes and macrophages are not the protective agent meant here

20385:
Close inbreeding raises homozygosity, so it is used to evolve purelines and to accumulate superior genes while eliminating undesirable ones
Prolonged inbreeding exposes harmful recessive alleles and lowers fertility and productivity through inbreeding depression

20386:
Sperm arise in the seminiferous tubules, drain into the rete testis and pass through the vasa efferentia to the epididymis for maturation and storage

20387:
With allele frequencies p + q = 1 the Hardy-Weinberg genotype frequencies are p^{2} + 2pq + q^{2} = 1

20388:
Pila is a mollusc feeding with a radula and Bombyx is an insect excreting through Malpighian tubules, giving the first two pairings
Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore swimming with comb plates and Taenia is a flatworm excreting through flame cells, giving the next two pairings

20389:
Chromosome arms are named by length, with the shorter arm called p and the longer arm called q

20390:
Flowering in photoperiod-sensitive plants is triggered by the relative duration of light and dark phases
The photoreceptive pigment phytochrome that measures this photoperiod is located in the leaves
The signal florigen then moves from the leaf to the shoot apex, so the leaf is the site of perception
→ (D)
20391:
Body temperature is held near its set point by sweating, shivering and blood flow adjustments
These autonomic responses are coordinated by the thermoregulatory centre in the hypothalamus of the forebrain
Cerebrum, corpus callosum and medulla do not serve as the thermostat, so the hypothalamus is the answer
→ (B)
20392:
Mitochondria and chloroplasts carry their own small circular DNA, and the nucleus lies within the nuclear envelope
Lysosomes are membrane sacs of digestive enzymes and vacuoles are storage sacs, and neither contains DNA
Hence the pair with no DNA in either member is lysosomes and vacuoles
→ (C)
20393:
The described individual is phenotypically male yet sterile with developed breast tissue
This matches Klinefelter syndrome with a 47,XXY complement, where the extra X causes small testes, gynaecomastia and sterility
Turner syndrome affects females while Edward and Down syndromes show different autosomal features, so Klinefelter fits
→ (B)
20394:
Xylem is the upward conducting tissue driven by transpiration pull from roots to shoots
Apart from water and dissolved mineral salts it also carries some organic nitrogen compounds and hormones upward
The option listing water, mineral salts, organic nitrogen and hormones together is therefore complete
→ (D)
20395:
Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-radiate it, warming the lower atmosphere
Carbon dioxide from fuel burning and methane from wetlands, paddies and livestock are the principal contributors among the choices
Ozone-ammonia, oxygen-nitrogen and nitrogen-sulphur dioxide pairs do not dominate this effect, so carbon dioxide and methane is correct
→ (D)
20396:
Chlorofluorocarbons released into the air destroy stratospheric ozone through chlorine radical reactions
The international agreement that scheduled the phase-out of CFC production and use was signed in Montreal
The Kyoto pact concerns greenhouse gases and the other listed protocols concern different issues, so the Montreal protocol is the answer
→ (A)
20397:
Development of an embryo from a female gamete without fusion of gametes occurs as asexual reproduction in some plants
This process is called parthenogenesis, while syngamy is fusion, autogamy is self-pollination and parthenocarpy is seedless fruit formation
Since the question specifies the egg itself forming the embryo with no fertilisation, parthenogenesis fits
→ (D)
20398:
Bacterial infections such as gonorrhoea and chlamydiasis are cured with antibiotics, and genital warts can be removed or managed
Genital herpes is caused by a virus that persists in nerve cells and recurs, so it cannot be fully eliminated
Among the listed diseases only genital herpes is therefore regarded as not completely curable
→ (C)
20399:
A transplanted kidney carries foreign antigens that the recipient immune system recognises as non-self
Graft rejection is driven chiefly by T lymphocytes that attack the foreign tissue, which is the cell-mediated arm of immunity
Humoral antibodies, autoimmunity and general inflammation do not define this rejection, so the cell-mediated response is correct
→ (D)
20400:
Concentrated urine requires reclaiming water from the tubular fluid against an osmotic gradient
The medullary interstitium is kept hyperosmotic toward the inner medulla by NaCl and urea countercurrent exchange
ADH only makes the collecting duct permeable while this gradient supplies the driving force
Low ADH therefore gives dilute urine and erythropoietin or filtration pressure do not concentrate it
→ (B)
20401:
A human insulin gene introduced into a bacterium is transcribed and translated by bacterial machinery
This succeeds because the same triplet codon specifies the same amino acid in nearly all organisms
Universality of the code lets the bacterial ribosome correctly read a human message
Lack of ambiguity or redundancy alone would not permit such cross-species expression
→ (C)
20402:
Lysosomes are single-membrane sacs filled with acid hydrolases active near pH 5
Their enzymes and membrane proteins are synthesised on the rough endoplasmic reticulum
Final glycosylation, tagging and packaging into vesicles takes place in the Golgi apparatus
Describing them as formed by packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum is therefore incorrect
→ (D)
20403:
Schleiden and Schwann established that cells are the structural and functional units of life
The refinement that every cell arises from a pre-existing cell was expressed as Omnis cellula-e cellula
This statement was first proposed by Rudolf Virchow in 1855
Neither Schwann, Schleiden nor Aristotle gave this formulation of cell division
→ (A)
20404:
Failing kidneys cannot hydroxylate vitamin D to calcitriol so calcium absorption from the gut falls
Diseased kidneys also secrete less erythropoietin so red cell production in marrow declines
Dialysis clears urea and balances potassium but does not replace these endocrine roles
Reduced calcium absorption with reduced RBC production is therefore the expected pair
→ (C)
20405:
Phloem carries sucrose from sources such as mature leaves to sinks such as roots, buds and fruits
Sink demand shifts with growth and season and source and sink roles can reverse
Sieve tubes must therefore move sugars upward to shoots and downward to roots as needed
Such source to sink movement in both directions is described as bidirectional
→ (D)
20406:
Tetany is hypocalcaemic hyperexcitability and botulism is toxin-induced paralysis
Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune block of neuromuscular transmission and none of these is inherited
Muscular dystrophy results from genetic defects of muscle proteins such as dystrophin
It passes from parents to offspring and is the inherited disorder in the list
→ (B)
20407:
Organ-system organisation with bilateral symmetry and a true coelom narrows the choice sharply
True segmentation into repeated metameres occurs in annelids, arthropods and chordates
Molluscs are organ-system grade, bilateral and coelomate yet unsegmented
Only the Annelida, Arthropoda and Chordata set carries all three characters
→ (A)
20408:
Morgan showed that genes lie linearly on chromosomes and exchange segments by crossing over
The nearer two genes lie, the rarer a crossover between them and the lower the recombinant frequency
Sturtevant proposed using recombination frequency as a measure of distance between genes
Mendel, Sutton-Boveri and Morgan himself did not formulate this mapping principle
→ (C)
20409:
Interphase precedes mitosis in the order growth, DNA synthesis, preparation and division
G_{1} carries growth and normal metabolism and is followed by S with genome duplication
G_{2} follows with synthesis of mitotic proteins and M closes the cycle with nuclear division
This G_{1} \rightarrow S \rightarrow G_{2} \rightarrow M sequence matches the stated option
→ (D)
20410:
Morels and truffles are prized edible ascomycetes and Claviceps yields ergot alkaloids including LSD
In most fungi asexual conidia are borne exogenously while ascospores form endogenously in asci
Yeasts are unicellular forms multiplying by budding and fission without a mycelium
Describing yeasts as filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae is therefore incorrect
→ (D)
20411:
Placentation describes the position where ovules attach inside the ovary
When ovules develop on the inner wall or on its peripheral cushion the condition is parietal
Axile bears them on a central axis, free central on a central column and basal at the base
Mustard and Argemone illustrate this parietal arrangement
→ (C)
20412:
The evil quartet lists habitat loss, overexploitation, alien invasion and coextinction as threats
Destruction and fragmentation remove area, niches and corridors on a continental scale
Drought, floods, exploitation and invasions matter locally but drive fewer global extinctions
Habitat loss and fragmentation is therefore ranked as the leading cause
→ (A)
20413:
Darwin emphasised small continuous directional variations shaped by natural selection
De Vries, studying Oenothera, proposed sudden large saltational changes by mutation
He held that such mutational variations arise by chance without a set direction
Random and directionless therefore captures his proposal on mutation
→ (B)
20414:
Respiratory quotient is the volume of CO_{2} released divided by O_{2} consumed
Carbohydrates give unity while organic acids exceed it and fats fall below it
Tripalmitin is a triglyceride whose poor oxygen content demands much inhaled oxygen
Its complete oxidation therefore gives an RQ near 0.7
→ (B)
20415:
Pink \text{F}_{1} from red \times white with intermediate phenotype is the classic incomplete dominance case in Antirrhinum
Selfing pink (Rr) gives genotypic and phenotypic ratio \frac{1}{4} Red : \frac{2}{4} Pink : \frac{1}{4} White, so dominance is absent but alleles still segregate unchanged into gametes
Hence the only false claim is that the law of segregation fails
→ (D)
20416:
Male Drosophila (XY) is heterogametic, male grasshoppers (XO) make half the sperms lacking a sex chromosome, and human males carry a short Y alongside X
In birds the female is heterogametic (ZW) while the male is homogametic (ZZ), so the sex of the chick is decided by the egg, not the sperm
Hence the statement assigning progeny sex to the sperm in fowls is incorrect
→ (C)
20417:
Interphase precedes mitosis in the order \text{G}_{1} growth then S DNA replication then \text{G}_{2} pre-mitotic growth
M phase follows interphase and completes the cycle before the next \text{G}_{1} begins
The only option reading \text{G}_{1} \rightarrow S \rightarrow \text{G}_{2} \rightarrow \text{M} is therefore correct
→ (D)
20418:
Thiobacillus denitrificans carries out denitrification, reducing nitrate to nitrite and then to free nitrogen gas released to the atmosphere
Nitrogen fixation is done by Rhizobium, Azotobacter and cyanobacteria, while nitrification of ammonia to nitrite to nitrate is done by Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter
Chemoautotrophic sulphur oxidation is a separate nutritional mode, not the process asked here
→ (D)
20419:
Polyblend is a fine powder of recycled and modified plastic waste blended with bitumen
This bitumen-polyblend mix laid for roads gives higher water repellency and load-bearing life, and was used experimentally at Bengaluru
It is not a fertilizer, sack material, or pipe material
→ (C)
20420:
Heterosporous pteridophytes such as Selaginella and Salvinia retain the female gametophyte on the parent sporophyte briefly while the young embryo develops
This retention with protection is the evolutionary precursor of the seed habit, carried further in gymnosperms
Bryophytes such as liverworts and mosses show a dominant gametophyte instead, so the first appearance is in pteridophytes
→ (C)
20421:
Human ribs comprise seven pairs of vertebrosternal true ribs, three pairs of vertebrochondral false ribs joining via cartilage, and two pairs of vertebral floating ribs with free ventral ends
The 8th to 10th pairs therefore do not articulate directly with the sternum, the 11th and 12th pairs have no sternal cartilage, and not every rib reaches the sternum ventrally
Only the seven-three-two classification is stated correctly
→ (D)
20422:
Concanavalin A is a globulin-type lectin obtained from jack bean seeds that agglutinates cells by binding specific carbohydrate residues
Lectins are classified among secondary metabolites alongside alkaloids and essential oils, but Concanavalin A itself belongs to the lectin group
It is neither an alkaloid, an essential oil, nor a pigment
→ (C)
20423:
The secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II and is released at ovulation in that state
Penetration of a sperm resumes meiosis II, and the second polar body is extruded after sperm entry but before the male and female pronuclei fuse
Completion after fertilization or before sperm entry or at first cleavage is therefore wrong
→ (A)
20424:
Pinus roots carry an obligate ectomycorrhizal association in which the fungal partner absorbs water and minerals while receiving photosynthate
Without this mycorrhizal partner the seedling cannot establish, even though the embryo is mature and the coat is not the barrier
No germination inhibitor is responsible for this dependence
→ (B)
20426:
Addition of chilled ethanol lowers the dielectric constant of the aqueous extract so that DNA salts precipitate as visible spoolable fibres
Isopropanol can also precipitate nucleic acids but the standard school protocol uses ice-cold ethanol after treatment with cellulase, protease and RNase
Methanol at room temperature and chilled chloroform do not serve this precipitation step
→ (B)
20427:
Bulliform motor cells in the upper epidermis of grass leaves lose turgor under water stress and turn flaccid
Their shrinkage rolls the lamina inwards, cutting transpiration during dry weather, and the leaf unrolls when turgor returns
Stomatal closure accompanies drought but the curling itself is driven by bulliform cells, not mesophyll shrinkage or tyloses
→ (B)
20428:
Crypts of Lieberkuhn are intestinal glands of the small intestine, the capsule covering the liver is Glisson capsule, and the Islets of Langerhans are the endocrine pancreas
Brunner glands of the duodenal submucosa complete the set
The full code matches the stated option
→ (C)
20429:
Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism with iodine deficiency enlarges the thyroid as goitre
Corticoid underproduction gives Addison disease and growth hormone excess after puberty gives acromegaly
The full code matches the stated option
→ (C)
20430:
Pills and emergency contraceptives are hormonal methods based on progesterone alone or combined progesterone-estrogen which suppress ovulation and alter cervical mucus and endometrium
Lactational amenorrhea works through hormonal control because high prolactin during intensive breastfeeding suppresses gonadotropin release and blocks ovulation
Barrier methods act mechanically while CuT acts through copper ions, so only lactational amenorrhea, pills and emergency contraceptives involve hormones
→ (A)
20431:
Morphine is the natural opiate obtained from poppy from which heroin is prepared by chemical modification of its two hydroxyl groups
Acetylation with acetic anhydride converts both hydroxyl groups into acetyl esters to give diacetylmorphine, which is heroin
Methylation, glycosylation and nitration do not yield this derivative, so heroin is synthesized by acetylation of morphine
→ (B)
20432:
The data show maximum survival of average-weight newborns near 3 to 3.3 kg and heavy mortality of both low-weight and high-weight extremes
Selection that favours the mean phenotype and removes both extremes is stabilizing selection, which keeps the population constant around the optimum
Directional selection shifts the mean one way and disruptive selection favours both extremes, so this pattern is stabilizing selection
→ (B)
20433:
The first step of glycolysis is phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate using ATP, and it is irreversible under cellular conditions
Hexokinase in most tissues and glucokinase in liver catalyze this priming phosphorylation of glucose
Aldolase, enolase and phosphofructokinase act later in the pathway, so the enzyme for glucose to glucose-6-phosphate is hexokinase
→ (B)
20434:
Cornea is the outer transparent protective covering of the eyeball that allows light entry and contributes to refraction
It is avascular rather than highly vascularised, so it receives nourishment from tears and aqueous humour and not from blood vessels
The given correct description among the choices is the external transparent protective covering, hence the first statement is accepted
→ (A)
20435:
Pyramids of energy are always upright because energy is lost at each transfer, while pyramids of numbers and biomass depend on standing crop
In the sea the producers are short-lived phytoplankton with very small standing biomass supporting larger zooplankton and fishes
Producer biomass therefore appears smaller than consumer biomass, so the pyramid of biomass in a sea is generally inverted
→ (D)
20436:
A tightly bound organic cofactor is called a prosthetic group, whereas metal ions associated with enzymes are described as cofactors or activators
Statement A is therefore incorrect because it extends the term prosthetic group to metal ions as well
A complete catalytically active enzyme with its bound cofactor is the holoenzyme, while apoenzyme is only the protein part, so statement B is also false
→ (C)
20437:
Wheezing with difficulty in breathing in polluted urban air describes asthma, an allergic respiratory disorder
It is caused by inflammation and reversible narrowing of bronchi and bronchioles with excess mucus and smooth muscle spasm
Nasal growths, alveolar fibrosis and surfactant deficiency describe different conditions, so the cause is inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles
→ (B)
20438:
After fertilization the ovary forms the fruit, the zygote forms the embryo and the central cell product forms the nutritive endosperm
Ovules are converted into seeds and the embryo sac is the pre-fertilization female gametophyte, not a post-fertilization product of ovules
Hence the statement that ovules develop into the embryo sac is the incorrect post-fertilization claim
→ (D)
20439:
Angiosperm phloem contains sieve tubes with companion cells along with sieve-tube elements, fibres and parenchyma
Gymnosperms possess the more primitive arrangement with sieve cells and albuminous cells instead
They therefore lack both sieve tubes and companion cells, which are restricted to angiosperms
→ (D)
20440:
Pineapple is a bromeliad with delayed natural flowering, so plant growth regulators are used to induce uniform flowering and improve yield
Auxin and ethylene, often applied as ethephon or NAA, promote flower initiation in pineapple throughout the year
Gibberellin, cytokinin and abscisic acid combinations do not give this commercial flowering response, so auxin and ethylene are used
→ (A)
20441:
The nucellus is the nutritive tissue surrounding the embryo sac inside the ovule and is usually consumed during seed development
When residual nucellus persists in the mature seed it forms a thin nutritive layer outside the endosperm
This persistent nucellus is termed perisperm, seen in seeds such as black pepper and beet
→ (B)
20442:
Actively dividing cells pass through interphase and mitosis, but some cells leave this rhythm under regulation
Cells entering \text{G}_{0} leave the cycle into a quiescent resting state and stop preparing for division
They may remain metabolically active there or re-enter on stimulus, so \text{G}_{0} cells exit the cell cycle
→ (A)
20443:
Saprophytes obtain nutrition by decomposition of dead organic matter, while parasites live on living plants or animals
Lichens are the symbiotic association of algae and fungi, and mycorrhiza is the symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots
The correct pairing is therefore a with ii, b with iii, c with iv and d with i
→ (D)
20445:
Bacillus thuringiensis produces inactive crystalline Cry protoxins
In the boll worm larva these crystals dissolve only in the alkaline pH of the midgut
Alkaline gut proteases then cleave the protoxin into the active toxin
The active toxin binds midgut epithelial cells and creates pores that swell and lyse the cells
Hence activation is triggered by the alkaline pH of the gut
→ (C)
20446:
Ciliated columnar epithelium beats coordinately to drive mucus or cells in one direction
In the bronchioles the cilia sweep mucus and trapped dust toward the pharynx
In the fallopian tubes the cilia move the ovum toward the uterus
Bile, pancreatic and salivary ducts lack this ciliated lining
So the pair present in humans is bronchioles and fallopian tubes
→ (D)
20447:
Each year cambium forms spring early wood with wide vessels and autumn late wood with narrow dense cells
Together they make one annual ring of light and dark bands
Cambial activity follows seasonal climate variation
Such sharp rings are prominent in temperate trees with distinct seasons and indistinct in tropical trees
So the statement that rings are not prominent in the temperate region is not true
→ (D)
20448:
The pollen tube discharges two male gametes into a synergid of the embryo sac
One male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form the diploid zygote
The second male gamete fuses with the two central cell nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus
This double fertilization matches one fusion with the egg and one with the central cell nuclei
→ (D)
20449:
The i gene codes for the lac repressor protein that binds the operator
The z gene codes for \beta-galactosidase which hydrolyses lactose into glucose and galactose
The y gene codes for permease which transports lactose into the cell
The a gene codes for transacetylase
This gives the stated matching code
→ (C)
20450:
Food passes from the mouth into the pharynx and then the oesophagus
The oesophagus opens into the large sac-like crop for storage
The crop leads into the muscular gizzard that grinds food with chitinous teeth
Behind the gizzard the hindgut runs as ileum then colon then rectum
This sequence matches crop before gizzard with ileum before colon before rectum
→ (A)
20451:
Homo habilis had a cranial capacity of about 650-800 cc
Homo erectus had a larger brain of about 900 cc
Homo neanderthalensis had a brain of about 1400 cc
Modern Homo sapiens averages about 1350 cc
This gives the stated matching code
→ (B)
20452:
Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi
Infection is confirmed by the Widal test which detects antibodies against the bacterial antigens
Plasmodium vivax causes malaria and Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia
Anthrone test detects carbohydrates and is unrelated to typhoid
So the correct pair is Salmonella typhi with the Widal test
→ (D)
20453:
Steroid hormones are lipid soluble and diffuse directly across the cell membrane
Inside the cell they bind an intracellular receptor to form a hormone-receptor complex
This complex enters the nucleus and binds specific DNA sequences to regulate gene expression
Membrane receptors with cyclic AMP as second messenger belong to peptide hormones
So steroid action works through binding to DNA as a gene-hormone complex
→ (B)
20454:
Expiratory capacity is the air exhaled after a normal inspiration
It equals tidal volume plus expiratory reserve volume
Substituting the values gives 500 \text{ mL} + 1000 \text{ mL} = 1500 \text{ mL}
Residual volume contributes only to functional residual capacity and total lung capacity
So the expiratory capacity is 1500 mL
→ (A)
20455:
Blood cholesterol synthesis proceeds through the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase
Statins obtained from yeast competitively inhibit this enzyme
This inhibition lowers blood cholesterol and is used commercially
Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant and streptokinase is a clot buster
So the cholesterol lowering agent is statin
→ (B)
20456:
The outer mitochondrial membrane carries porins permeable to small monomers
The inner membrane is folded into cristae that bear the electron transport enzymes and ATP synthase
The matrix holds a single circular DNA molecule with ribosomes for partial autonomy
Placing the electron transport enzymes in the outer membrane is therefore wrong
The incorrect statement is the one about the outer membrane
→ (B)
20457:
The P wave records depolarisation of the atria
The QRS complex records depolarisation of the ventricles with atrial repolarisation hidden within it
The T wave records repolarisation of the ventricles
A reduction in the size of the T wave signals coronary ischemia
This gives the stated matching code with the T change linked to ischemia
→ (A)
20458:
Biocontrol agents are organisms that attack plant pathogens and insect pests
Trichoderma is a free living fungus used against soil borne plant pathogens
Baculoviruses kill specific insect pests and Bacillus thuringiensis supplies insecticidal Cry proteins
Mosaic virus is a pathogen while aphids and biofertilizer genera are not biocontrol agents
→ (B)
20459:
Botanical names use a capitalized genus with a lowercase species epithet
The mango described by Linnaeus is Mangifera indica
The author citation is abbreviated as Linn. after the binomial
The form with capital Indica or with Car. Linn. is incorrect
So the correctly written name is Mangifera indica Linn.
→ (B)
